passage: Snow was piling against the window of the Toronto flat when Tariq came back from his shift. "Oh, you're home," Amira said. "Thought you might stay out with your new favourite coworker." She laughed, but it came out thin. Tariq frowned and put the groceries down. Later she took her plate to the bedroom and shut the door, waiting to see if he would knock. He did, after twenty minutes, looking tired. While he showered, his phone lit up on the bed. Her hand hovered. She picked it up, read nothing but a delivery message, and felt no better at all. When he came out, he saw the phone in a different spot. He said nothing, and the silence sat between them all evening.

qa.q: Where did Tariq's phone light up?
qa.a: His phone lit up on the bed while he showered.

qa.q: Why did Amira shut the bedroom door with her plate?
qa.a: She wanted to test whether Tariq would come after her, hoping it would prove he still cared.

qa.q: What turning point is available for Amira now?
qa.a: Instead of more tests, she could tell Tariq plainly that she has been feeling insecure, because the checks are not calming her and are starting to hurt him.

qa.q: How is Tariq likely experiencing these tests?
qa.a: He seems worn out and uneasy; the joke, the closed door and the moved phone may make him feel watched and distrusted. 😔

grounding: It shows a young woman using half-joking jabs, withdrawal to see if he follows, and a phone check that brings no reassurance and strains both people.

passage: The hostel common room was empty except for Himani and Parth, sharing a packet of chips before the library closed. "So, is your lab partner coming to the fest too?" she asked, grinning a little too wide. "Maybe you two can present together, you're such a team." Parth laughed awkwardly. "Himani, she's just my lab partner." "Relax, I'm joking." Her friend Pallavi, passing with a laundry bucket, caught Himani's eye and raised an eyebrow. Later Himani didn't answer Parth's goodnight text, just to see if he'd call. He called twice, then stopped. Next morning he looked like he hadn't slept. "Are we okay?" he asked, and she heard herself say, "You tell me."

qa.q: Where were Himani and Parth sharing chips?
qa.a: They were in the hostel common room.

qa.q: What might Himani want when she ignores Parth's goodnight text?
qa.a: She seems to want proof that he cares enough to chase her, because she is afraid of losing him to his lab partner.

qa.q: What could turn things around for Himani at this stage?
qa.a: She could drop the half jokes and the silence and tell Parth honestly that she feels insecure, so he is not left guessing.

qa.q: What is it like for Parth right now?
qa.a: He looks sleepless and unsure, asking "Are we okay?" because the jokes and silence leave him worried without knowing why.

grounding: It illustrates provoking with teasing remarks and pulling away to test the partner, which wears both of them down.
